+# AGENTS
+
+## Project Context
+
+### Tech Stack
+
+- `tshy` for building typescript
+- `tap` for testing
+- `npm` for package management and running project scripts
+- `oxlint` for linting
+- `prettier` for formatting
+
+### Purpose
+
+- A fast and featureful bash-compatible glob matcher in
+  JavaScript
+
+### Structure
+
+- `./src/*.ts` Source files
+- `./test/*.ts` Tap test files
+- `./test/fixtures/` test fixtures
+- `./scripts/` various project scripts
+
+## Critical Commands
+
+- Running tests: `npm test`
+- Running tests, updating snapshots: `npm snap`
+- Building code: `npm run prepare`
+- Running benchmarks: `npm run bench`
+- Linting: `npm run lint`
+- Formatting code: `npm run format`
+- Regenerating Bash behavior test fixtures: `npm run test-regen`
+  **IMPORTANT** This should _only_ be run on systems with a
+  recent `Bash 5.3` build as the default `bash` binary.
+- Benchmarking: `npm run bench`
+- Benchmarking in a Docker container that is limited to 4 CPUs
+  and 8GB of memory, with the median of 3 runs:
+  `npm run bench:docker` (set `BENCH_RUNS`, `BENCH_CPUS`, and
+  `BENCH_MEMORY` to change these)
+- Profiling: `npm run prof`
+- Generating docs: `npm run typedoc`
+
+## Coding Standards & Rules
+
+### Language
+
+Use TypeScript exclusively; avoid `any`.
+
+### Code Organization
+
+Every class must be in its own css-case-named file under `src`.
+For example, a class named `AsyncHookManager` would live in
+`src/async-hook-manager.ts`.
+
+### DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)
+
+Do not duplicate functions, methods, or objects unnecessarily.
+
+Prefer to consolidate and reuse code whenever possible.
+
+**NEVER** add new methods, objects, or functions, without
+explicit human direction. When asked to do so, make the
+_smallest_ possible increase to the API surface area.
+
+### Testing
+
+- 100% test coverage is critically important.
+- Every patch **must** include a test that fails without the
+  patch, and passes with the patch.
+- Tests should be human readable.
+- Prefer adding to an existing set of test cases rather than
+  writing a new test, if possible.
+- All new features require matching tests in the `/tests`
+  directory.
+- Run `npm test` before proposing a solution to ensure no
+  regressions.
+- Mock external API calls using `t.mockImport`.
+
+### Documentation
+
+Export all types.
+
+Every public method and option must have a JSDoc comment.
+
+### Commit Messages
+
+Do not use "semantic commits". Whether it is a feature, fix, or
+chore, should be evident from context.
+
+The first line of the commit message should summarize the change
+in less than 50 characters
+
+Write commit messages in the present tense imperative voice,
+describing what the patch does without qualifiers or referring to
+the patch itself. For example: `add whiz deduplication for
+performance`, not `patch adds whiz deduplication, which should
+improve performance somewhat`.
+
+The body of the commit message, if necessary, should explain the
+reasoning behind the change, with hard line-breaks at 80
+characters.
+
+If there are breaking behavior changes for users, these **MUST**
+be described in the commit message body.
+
+The commit message should only very rarely mention the
+implementation – that should be evident from the code change
+itself. However, it _may_ be worthwhile to explain _why_ a given
+implementation is chosen, when alternatives exist.
+
+Commit messages, like code, should be as minimal as possible to
+accomplish their goal.
+
+- **NEVER** link to or reference IDs of bugs, issues, or other
+  objects in issue trackers other than the GitHub issue tracker
+  for this repository.
+- **DO** include a `fix: #1234` link to any GitHub issues that
+  this patch fixes, or `re: #1234` link to any GitHub issues or
+  pull requests that are relevant to this change.
+
+## Boundaries & Guardrails
+
+- **DO NOT** modify anything in the `/scripts` directory.
+- **DO NOT** commit secrets or `.env` files.
+- **NEVER** use `force` flags when running Git commands.
+- If a task requires a new dependency, ask the human to perform
+  the command.
+- **DO NOT** modify `package.json` or `package-lock.json`.
+- Run `npm run bench` before and after any significant patches,
+  to ensure that there are no performance regressions.

+## ReDoS Protection
+
+Many glob implementations make a regular expression from each
+pattern. A pattern such as `a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a`, tested against
+a name such as `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaab` that does not
+match, can make a backtracking regular expression engine try each
+way that the `*` characters can split the name. The time that
+this takes grows exponentially with the length of the name, so a
+pattern from an untrusted source can stop a process for minutes
+or more. This is a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS).
+
+This module never makes a regular expression from a pattern.
+Each portion of a pattern between `/` characters that has magic
+is matched by a `Matcher` from
+[@isaacs/nonrecursive-glob-match](http://npm.im/@isaacs/nonrecursive-glob-match).
+A `Matcher` is not a `RegExp`, and it does not backtrack. It tests
+all of the ways that the pattern can match at the same time, in
+one pass over the name, so no pattern can make it try the ways one
+after another. The time to match a name grows no faster than its
+length times the size of the portion of the pattern, for each
+kind of pattern, including nested and negated extglobs such as
+`+(a|*(b|!(c)))`. The pattern above matches or fails in about a
+millisecond.
+
+The only regular expressions that a `Matcher` uses are for `[...]`
+classes and case folding, and each of them only tests one
+character at a time, so they can not backtrack over a name.
+

+
+- The states that a `Matcher` reaches are cached, so that names
+  are matched faster, but the cache has a fixed size. When it is
+  full, it is cleared.

+  use an unbounded amount of memory.

+  throws an error.

+  each other is matched with a limit on how deeply minimatch
+  recurses (200 by default). Past that limit, a path is not
+  treated as a match, so that path is not ignored.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Run the benchmarks in a Docker container that is limited to a set
+# number of CPUs and amount of memory, so that the results depend
+# less on what else the machine is doing. The fixture is in a tmpfs
+# in the container, so the results do not depend on the disk either.
+# This is for comparing the implementations with each other: the
+# times are for Linux in a container, and not for the host.
+#
+# The settings, and their defaults:
+#   BENCH_RUNS=3    the number of times to run benchmark.sh. Each
+#                   result is the median of the runs.
+#   BENCH_CPUS=4    the number of CPUs that the container can use
+#   BENCH_MEMORY=8g the memory that the container can use, with no
+#                   swap
+
+set -e
+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
+
+runs=${BENCH_RUNS:-3}
+cpus=${BENCH_CPUS:-4}
+memory=${BENCH_MEMORY:-8g}
+
+npm run prepare >&2
+
+# the build context: the built glob and its dependencies, and the
+# benchmark scripts
+ctx=$(mktemp -d)
+trap '[ -n "$ctx" ] && rm -rf "$ctx"' EXIT
+node bench-docker/stage.mjs "$ctx/glob" >&2
+cp benchmark.sh patterns.sh make-benchmark-fixture.sh "$ctx/"
+mkdir -p "$ctx/bench-docker"
+cp bench-docker/run.sh bench-docker/summary.mjs "$ctx/bench-docker/"
+
+docker build -q -t glob-bench -f bench-docker/Dockerfile "$ctx" >&2
+
+docker run --rm \
+  --cpus="$cpus" \
+  --cpuset-cpus="0-$((cpus - 1))" \
+  --memory="$memory" \
+  --memory-swap="$memory" \
+  --tmpfs /glob/bench-working-dir/fixture:rw,exec,size=2g,nr_inodes=1000000 \
+  glob-bench "$runs"

+// Copy the built glob package, and the packages that it needs at run
+// time, into a folder that can be a Docker build context.
+//
+// Only the `dependencies` of each package are followed, and only its
+// published files (package.json and its `files` list) are copied, so
+// that a package that is linked to a local checkout does not bring
+// its dev dependencies or sources with it. Each dependency is found
+// the same way that Node finds it, from the folder of the package
+// that needs it.
+//
+// usage: node bench-docker/stage.mjs <dest>
+
+import {
+  cpSync,
+  existsSync,
+  mkdirSync,
+  readFileSync,
+  realpathSync,
+} from 'fs'
+import { dirname, join, relative, resolve, sep } from 'path'
+
+const dest = process.argv[2]
+if (!dest) throw new Error('usage: stage.mjs <dest>')
+
+const readPkg = dir =>
+  JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
+
+// the real folder of the package `name`, as Node finds it from `from`
+const find = (name, from) => {
+  for (let d = from; ; d = dirname(d)) {
+    const pj = join(d, 'node_modules', name, 'package.json')
+    if (existsSync(pj)) return realpathSync(dirname(pj))
+    if (dirname(d) === d)
+      throw new Error(`cannot find ${name} from ${from}`)
+  }
+}
+
+// copy the published files of the package in `src` to `to`
+const copyPkg = (src, to) => {
+  mkdirSync(to, { recursive: true })
+  const pkg = readPkg(src)
+  cpSync(join(src, 'package.json'), join(to, 'package.json'))
+  const files = pkg.files ?? ['.']
+  for (const f of files) {
+    if (!existsSync(join(src, f))) continue
+    cpSync(join(src, f), join(to, f), {
+      recursive: true,
+      dereference: true,
+      // the package's own node_modules, not the one it is in
+      filter: s => !relative(src, s).split(sep).includes('node_modules'),
+    })
+  }
+}
+
+// The packages are placed in the top level node_modules, unless a
+// different copy with the same name is already there. Then it is
+// placed in the node_modules of the package that needs it.
+const placed = new Map()
+const stage = (src, to, top) => {
+  copyPkg(src, to)
+  for (const name of Object.keys(readPkg(src).dependencies ?? {})) {
+    const dep = find(name, src)
+    const atTop = placed.get(name)
+    if (atTop === dep) continue
+    if (atTop === undefined) {
+      placed.set(name, dep)
+      stage(dep, join(top, 'node_modules', name), top)
+    } else {
+      stage(dep, join(to, 'node_modules', name), top)
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+const root = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..')
+stage(root, resolve(dest), resolve(dest))
+for (const [name, dir] of placed) console.log(`${name} <- ${dir}`)

+// Print the median of each result over several runs of benchmark.sh,
+// in the same format, and the total time of each implementation over
+// all of the patterns.
+//
+// usage: node bench-docker/summary.mjs <output file> ...
+
+import { readFileSync } from 'fs'
+
+const files = process.argv.slice(2)
+// pattern -> section -> name -> [times], counts. A pattern can be in
+// the list more than once, so they are keyed by their place in it.
+const results = new Map()
+for (const f of files) {
+  let pattern = ''
+  let n = 0
+  let section = ''
+  for (const line of readFileSync(f, 'utf8').split('\n')) {
+    const p = line.match(/^--- pattern: '(.*)' ---$/)
+    if (p) {
+      pattern = `${n++}\0${p[1]}`
+      continue
+    }
+    const s = line.match(/^~~ (.*) ~~$/)
+    if (s) {
+      section = s[1]
+      continue
+    }
+    const r = line.match(/^(.+?)\s*\t(\d+)m([\d.]+)s\s+(\d+)/)
+    if (!r || !pattern) continue
+    const [, name, min, sec, count] = r
+    const byName = results.get(pattern) ?? new Map()
+    results.set(pattern, byName)
+    const key = `${section}\0${name.trim()}`
+    const row = byName.get(key) ?? { times: [], counts: new Set() }
+    byName.set(key, row)
+    row.times.push(Number(min) * 60 + Number(sec))
+    row.counts.add(count)
+  }
+}
+
+const median = a => {
+  const s = [...a].sort((x, y) => x - y)
+  return s[s.length >> 1]
+}
+const fmt = t => `${Math.floor(t / 60)}m${(t % 60).toFixed(3)}s`
+
+const totals = new Map()
+console.log(`median of ${files.length} runs\n`)
+for (const [pattern, byName] of results) {
+  console.log(`--- pattern: '${pattern.split('\0')[1]}' ---`)
+  let section = ''
+  for (const [key, { times, counts }] of byName) {
+    const [sec, name] = key.split('\0')
+    if (sec !== section) console.log(`~~ ${(section = sec)} ~~`)
+    const m = median(times)
+    totals.set(key, (totals.get(key) ?? 0) + m)
+    const count =
+      counts.size === 1 ? [...counts][0] : [...counts].join('/')
+    console.log(`${name.padEnd(25)}\t${fmt(m)}  ${count}`)
+  }
+  console.log()
+}
+console.log('--- total of the medians ---')
+for (const [key, t] of totals) {
+  const [sec, name] = key.split('\0')
+  console.log(`${`${name} (${sec})`.padEnd(36)}\t${t.toFixed(3)}s`)
+}

+import { bashResults } from './bash-results.js'
+import { same } from 'tcompare'
+const globs = Object.keys(bashResults)
+
+const testNativeGlob = !!Number(process.env.TEST_NATIVE_GLOB ?? '0')
+
+if (!fs.glob || !fs.globSync || !fsp.glob) {
+  t.plan(0, 'This version of node does not include fs.glob')
+  process.exit(testNativeGlob ? 1 : 0)
+}
+
+// run from the root of the project
+// this is usually where you're at anyway, but be sure.
+const __dirname = fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url))
+const fixtures = resolve(__dirname, 'fixtures')
+process.chdir(fixtures)
+
+const alphasort = (a: string, b: string) =>
+  a.toLowerCase().localeCompare(b.toLowerCase(), 'en')
+
+const cleanResults = (m: string[]) => {
+  // normalize discrepancies in ordering, duplication,
+  // and ending slashes.
+  return m
+    .map(m => m.replace(/\/$/, ''))
+    .sort(alphasort)
+    .reduce((set: string[], f) => {
+      if (f !== set[set.length - 1]) set.push(f)
+      return set
+    }, [])
+    .map(f => {
+      // de-windows
+      return process.platform !== 'win32' ?
+          f

+    })
+    .sort(alphasort)

+  // anything regarding the symlink thing will fail on windows
